    Search changeset comments

    Source: R/osmapi_changeset_discussion.R
    osm_search_comment_changeset_discussion.Rd

    Returns changeset comments that match the specified query. If no query is provided, the most recent changeset comments are returned.

    Usage

    osm_search_comment_changeset_discussion(
  user,
  from,
  to,
  format = c("R", "xml", "json"),
  tags_in_columns = FALSE
)

    Arguments

    user

    Search for changeset comments created by the user with the given user id (numeric) or display name (character).

    from

    Beginning date range. See details for the valid formats.

    to

    End date range. Only works when from is supplied. See details for the valid formats.

    format

    Format of the output. Can be "R" (default), "xml", or "json".

    tags_in_columns

    If FALSE (default), the tags of the changesets are saved in a single list column tags containing a data.frame for each changeset with the keys and values. If TRUE, add a column for each key. Ignored if format != "R".

    Value

    If format = "R", returns a data frame with one comment per If format = "xml", returns a xml2::xml_document. If format = "json", returns a list with the json structure.

    Details

    The valid formats for from and to parameters are POSIXt values or characters preferably in ISO 8601 format.

    See also

    Other changeset discussion's functions: osm_comment_changeset_discussion(), osm_hide_comment_changeset_discussion(), osm_subscribe_changeset_discussion()

    Examples

    # See the latest changeset comments globally:
osm_search_comment_changeset_discussion()
#>          id                date visible      uid                  user

#> 15  Hi Matthew, thanks for getting back to us. A zero-hour block is put in place when a mapper is making errors and not responding to comments or communications trying to establish a dialog. The block is immediately lifted once communication is established. Please make sure you can receive notification emails that are sent to your account.\n\nDid you have a chance to read over the wiki page mentioned above? You are asking if we don't want fairway objects tagged as fairway objects. That's not at all the situation. Maybe I need to work on that wiki page further. Your workflow of drawing the fairway to include the fringe around the green and make the green the inner boundary of a multipolygon is correct. But that's where you should stop. You are then setting the outer boundary as a fairway as well. What that says is that *everything* within that boundary is a fairway, overriding the fact that the relation has already established that the fairway exists every except the green. It's just mathematically incorrect to say that.\n\nAnd yes, iD doesn't handle areas vs. closed polygons well. You could always try submitting a request for new features, but I think you'd be better off switching to a more advanced editor like JOSM. It will give you much better visualizations of multipolygons for starters. And yes, it is FOSS.\n\nAs a side note, I see that you selected several different fairway/green pairs and joined them into a monolithic multipolygon in the last 48 hours. You should avoid doing that. Stick to just fairway/green/bunkers that are contained in a single fairway. While not explicitly called out as wrong, it isn't done anywhere else in the country is probably should be addressed as something to avoid.\n\nI'm always happy to help people map golf courses better. Please feel free to reach out and ask further questions if needed.

#> 43                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  I was actually searching for that hotel recently, but because it had been deleted, I couldn't find it. Using lifecycle tags (like disused:tourism=hotel or construction:tourism=hotel) makes things much easier. Once work is finished, someone can simply update a single tag to reactivate it—without having to re-position it or hunt down the contact details again.\n\nIt also brings a few other big benefits:\n\n    Prevents duplicate mapping: A lifecycle tag clearly signals to other mappers that the POI is tracked, stopping people from accidentally re-creating it or wondering why it vanished.\n\n    Better for app users: It lets data consumers know the location actually exists but is temporarily inactive, rather than making OSM look like it's missing data.\n\n    Preserves history: It keeps local context visible on the map layer so future contributors don't have to dig through old node revision histories.\n\nThat's why the community relies so much on lifecycle prefixes for temporary closures—it saves a lot of work and keeps the map accurate!
